quest.title: Wines of Mondstadt
quest.description: The business has always been good at Angel's Share. However, Charles the bartender seems to be troubled by something recently...
quest.rewards_formatted: Suspicious Steak x3, Cecilia x8, Apple x18, Stained Mask x3, Delicious "Pile 'Em Up" x2, Windwheel Aster x6, Wolfhook x12, Heavy Horn x2, Fried Radish Balls x3, Dandelion Seed x4, Sunsettia x12, Damaged Mask x4, Steak x6, Sweet Flower x6, Berry x6, Slime Condensate x2, Sausage x1, Ham x1

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: I wonder if I should tell Master Diluc...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Here's the thing. The Angel's Share was built by the Dawn Winery, and only their very finest alcoholic beverages are served here.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Mondstadt is home to many taverns, but the Angel's Share is by all accounts the best in the city.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Everyone has their favorite tipple, of course, and when we first started we could cater to everyone's preferences. But the more customers we get, the more difficult that becomes...

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: I want to suggest to Master Diluc to have the winery come up with some new flavors of wine, so that we don't start losing customers.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: But even if he were to agree, developing new products takes time. And I also have no idea what kind of things Mondstadters like to drink these days.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: I heard about the <color=#00E1FFFF>Four Drunkards of Mondstadt</color>, so I am wondering about getting their input first.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, can you convince one of the <color=#00E1FFFF>Drunkards</color> to come to the tavern?

response.speaker: Charles
response.text: You have my thanks. Hope you find one of the <color=#00E1FFFF>Drunkards</color> soon.

response.speaker: Charles
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you aren't at drinking age yet — are you?

response.speaker: Charles
response.text: In which case, I presume you know precious little about alcohol-related matters. You should ask the experts instead...

response.speaker: Charles
response.text: If you don't know where to find the Drunkards, ask Nimrod. His affection for alcohol is widely renowned... Anything to do with drinking, he's sure to know about it.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: That Eury, I mean seriously...

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are the Four Drunkards?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: You want to know about the Drunkards? You're not old enough to drink though, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: I suppose that doesn't stop me from telling you their story though.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: There are four people in Mondstadt recognized as absolute champions of alcohol consumption, both in terms of the quantity and quality of what they drink. We call them the Four Drunkards.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Now, try not to be too alarmed when I tell you their names, they might be people you know...

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: First off we've got <color=#00E1FFFF>Quinn</color>, who runs the fruit stall down near the city gates. He is something of a fruit wine aficionado, which is why he's so picky about the quality of fruit he sells at his stall, too.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Next you've got <color=#00E1FFFF>Margaret</color>, who is often seen strolling the streets. Her idea of what "dandelion wine" is, is on a whole other level compared to what it means to most people.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Then there's <color=#00E1FFFF>Jack </color> from down town Mondstadt. You must run into him all the time? No one loves a beer quite as much as Jack.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Last but not least is the jagerschnapps meister himself... That is, the expert on distilled spirits, <color=#00E1FFFF>Draff</color> of Springvale. No surprises there, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: So there you go, that's Mondstadt's Four Drunkards! Any more questions?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All clear.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: So there you go, that's Mondstadt's Four Drunkards! If you want my advice, I'd suggest you talk to <color=#00E1FFFF>Draff</color> in <color=#00E1FFFF>Springvale</color>. He's always happy to talk about anything alcohol related!

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Anyway, you'll find all the other Drunkards in <color=#00E1FFFF>Mondstadt</color> too. It's up to you which one to go looking for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's mix some drinks...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: The Drunkards— Shh! This is a public place!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Yes, I do know a thing or two about fruit wine. But you ask me to go and mix drinks with you when I have to watch my fruit stall...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Drunkards...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Shut up! I told you already, not in public! You're a liability you are... Alright, I'll head to the Angel's Share shortly.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: But since it was you who offered to mix drinks, I'll leave it to you to fetch the ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Let me think... <color=#00E1FFFF>Apples</color> are my go-to when mixing drinks. Meet me at the Angel's Share when you've found some.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Want to mix some drinks?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Drunkards, eh. That's... one way of putting it. So, you want to mix some drinks with me?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: But why me? You know I run the Cat's Tail and the Angel's Share is our biggest rival, right?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Calm down, I'm only kidding! One doesn't seriously consider trying to rival the Angel's Share when they have the backing of the Dawn Winery...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Anyway, mixing drinks at the Angel's Share sounds quite fun.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: I'll head over there while you grab some ingredients. Let me see... Dandelion wine is their house special...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Yes, go and collect some <color=#00E1FFFF>dandelions</color> for me.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: We serve dandelion wine too, but it's quite different. Once you've got the dandelions, meet me at the Angel's Share.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's make cocktails!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Cocktails? Pff! I don't drink cocktails!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: I drink my alcohol straight, nothing added, so I can actually taste it! It's the only way to drink.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: But I can come along and give you a few tips. Show you how a real hunter drinks!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Before you go to the Angel's Share, though, pick up some <color=#00E1FFFF>berries</color> for me on the way.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: What for? You'll have to wait and see.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Want to mix a drink?

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: I... don't really know how. And in any case, have you ever heard of anybody mixing with beer?

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: That said, I do know the secret to a better-tasting beer. Firstly, you need a friend you can clink glasses with...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Beer tastes best after you've clinked glasses with a friend. It's a taste you can't beat, however you want to mix it. That's why adventurers love it.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Alright, don't give me that look! You have a fair few friends, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Tell you what, I'll meet you halfway. If you find me some <color=#00E1FFFF>sweet flowers</color>, I'll meet you at the Angel's Share. Sound good?

talks.objective: Ask one of the drunkards about the signature cocktail

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}. You're back.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here are the mixing ingredients.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: What are you planning on making with these!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me give it a little thought...

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: If you're unsure, you're better off talking to the Drunkard to refresh your memory.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: It's hard to please everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: #Hang on, let {NICKNAME} mix this one. I'll watch and give some instructions.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: I've made this drink more times than I can remember and I'm a bit sick of it.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: I can't fault it — it's just nothing new to me.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Traveler, I assume you've never had an alcoholic drink before, let alone mixed one?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Who knows — maybe your fresh take on drink mixing could produce something unexpectedly delicious!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: I was planning on making a Mondstadt Sunset. It has a jagerschnapps base and uses apple juice.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: First you need to squeeze the fruit juice into the base liquor. Then give it a good shake followed by a thorough stir to really mix the liquor and the fruit juice together.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Lastly, let it sit for a while. This gives time for the pulp, and any juices that didn't mix properly, to settle.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Through the side of the glass you can see the brilliant brightness of the fruit juices congregating towards the very bottom, just like the setting sun. Hence the name, "Mondstadt Sunset."

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Time for you to give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: #Eh... I'd rather let {NICKNAME} have a go of mixing this one.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: There's nothing new about dandelion wine, even if my mixing method is a little unorthodox. The flavor is broadly the same.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: But after all, it is Mondstadt's signature wine. That much will never change, regardless of any variations in flavor and texture.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: So let's have the traveler try their hand at making this one. Maybe there is still something new for you to unearth in this mainstay of Mondstadt's wine scene.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: First I'll talk you through how to mix my special concoction, the Margaret. Hmm... it's essentially an alternative-style dandelion wine.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: The base of the Margaret is jagerschnapps. The other main ingredient is Dandelion Seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: First, stir the jagerschnapps until it has an even composition, and add in the dandelion seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Next, give it a good shake. This lets air mix with the jagerschnapps and helps it absorb the refreshing flavor of the dandelion seeds.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Finally, let it sit a while; the impurities will sink to the bottom while the dandelion seeds rise to the top. Then enjoy the refreshing blast on the tip of your tongue as you down it in one... And there you have it, my signature concoction.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Now, give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: #Come on {NICKNAME}, let me see you mix a drink.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Don't look so shell-shocked... I say mix a drink, but really what's there to mix?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: The best way to enjoy the flavor is to drink it straight. The way it comes out the bottle!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Then again... If you keep that up for too long, it starts to affect your ability to stand up...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: How about this, traveler: Mix me a random drink, preferably one I've never seen before.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Oh, and I almost forgot — let me tell you how a hunter drinks.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: You have some berries? Good, put them to one side for now.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Pour yourself a glass of jagerschnapps, then go and do whatever... In any case, let it sit there until you think it's been long enough.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Then put the ready-to-eat berries in the glass and down it in one!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: You must make sure that the berry juice and the alcohol enter your mouth together.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Haha, with a glass of that inside me I'm ready to make a charged attack on any prey that comes my way.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: That's all there is to it. Now, get mixing!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: #This looks like a job for {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Don't be nervous. Beer doesn't need mixing; at most it just needs a minor tweak to how it's made.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: The thing that impacts the flavor of beer the most? That would be the person you're drinking it with, naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Hahaha. But on a more serious note, the main factor influencing the taste is, of course, the head.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: It forms from the beer splashing when you're pulling a pint, it also forms when you agitate your glass as you're clinking it, and you can smear it on your friend's face to liven things up a little.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: My way of serving beer is very simple. It just takes beer and sweet flower.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Firstly, put the sweet flower in the bottom of a glass, then pour the beer over it. Shake it up a bit to work up a head.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Then take a sip, and you should be able to get some of the head and a bit of sweet flower.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: If you clink glasses with a friend, the frothy head splashes out in little pearly beads. That's why we dub it a Pearl Ale.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: What do you think? Pretty easy, huh? Now, give it a go!

talks.objective: Give the cocktail ingredients to Charles

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Hmm... I need to think what drink to make...

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: #Well, if that's the case, I look forward to your mixological creation, {NICKNAME}!

talks.objective: Progress in helping Charles collect information

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: All the prep is done, it's time to get mixing.

talks.objective: Talk to Charles and prepare to make a cocktail
Talk to Charles and finish the cocktail

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jagerschnapps

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: A fiery liquor used as a go-to cocktail base throughout the city. The cautious choice.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Beer

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Beer? A fair choice, quick and easy and widely appreciated. ...But can you really mix with beer?

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Okay, so the base is decided.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Add ingredients

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: The ingredients are good to go. Let's add them in.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: What's the next step?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Shake

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Nice! That was a good hard shake, it looks like it's all blended very nicely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Stir

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Good... Yes, just like that. Your stirring technique is not bad.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let it sit

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Okay, leave it here then. Sometime playing the waiting game is part of the mixing process.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Hmm... Not bad, not bad...

talks.objective: Ask Charles about his opinion on cocktails

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: I wonder how well this drink will be received...

talks.objective: Give the cocktail to Quinn to try

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: It looks good! I really want to try it...

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Anyway. I will see what other people have to say about this drink first.

talks.objective: Give the cocktail to Margaret to try

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'm sure someone out there will probably like it...

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Anyway. I will see what other people have to say about this drink first.

talks.objective: Give the cocktail to Draff to try

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I want to start again.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Start a new drink from scratch? Be my guest.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: There are still some leftover ingredients, but there isn't time to prepare anything new.

talks.objective: Give the cocktail to Jack to try

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Let's leave it there for today. I look forward to your next concoction.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Honestly, the quality of today's batch...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: #Oh, hi {NICKNAME}. Can I help you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Oh... I was hoping you were here to buy some fruit. Goodbye then.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Prince has run off again...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: #Eh? {NICKNAME}, did you want something? If you want a drink, feel free to just go to the tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Goodbye. You should stop in at the Cat's Tail some time when you're free.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Hunters, hurry!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Are you here for some game?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Goodbye. If you ever want any hunting produce, I'm your guy!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: When will the next adventure be...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Any new stories to tell me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: I thought you had some exciting adventure stories to tell me. Well, bye.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: It looks like you persuaded one of the Drunkards to come here.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Once they've arrived, let's start mixing some drinks.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Hello? What is it?

choices.text: Remind me how to mix a Mondstadt Sunset.

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: The base of a Mondstadt Sunset is jagerschnapps. You also need apples.

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: First you need to squeeze the fruit juice into the base liquor. Then give it a good shake followed by a thorough stir to really mix the liquor and the fruit juice together.

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: Lastly, let it sit for a while. This gives time for the pulp, and any juices that didn't mix properly, to settle.

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: And there you have it, a Mondstadt Sunset. Any more questions?

response.speaker: Quinn
response.text: Have a try, and if you have any more questions, I'll be right here.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

choices.text: Remind me how to mix a Margaret.

response.speaker: Margaret
response.text: The base of the Margaret is jagerschnapps. The other main ingredient is dandelion seeds.

response.speaker: Margaret
response.text: First, stir the jagerschnapps until it has an even composition, and add in the dandelion seeds.

response.speaker: Margaret
response.text: Next, give it a good shake. This lets air mix with the jagerschnapps and helps it absorb the refreshing flavor of the dandelion seeds.

response.speaker: Margaret
response.text: Finally, let it sit a while so the impurities sink to the bottom and the dandelion seeds rise to the top.

response.speaker: Margaret
response.text: And that, my friend, is how Margaret mixes a Margaret!

response.speaker: Margaret
response.text: I can't wait to see how yours turns out.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Hmm? Did you want something?

choices.text: Remind me how to mix a Charged Attack.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Simple — it's just jagerschnapps and berries. Have you forgotten already?

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Leave the jagerschnapps to sit until you're ready for it, then add in the berries.

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Got it? Then get to it!

response.speaker: Draff
response.text: Get to work on that drink. I'm waiting!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Do you need to recap anything?

choices.text: Remind me how to mix a Pearl Ale.

response.speaker: Jack
response.text: Oh. You forgot? No worries, let's go over it again.

response.speaker: Jack
response.text: All you need is beer and sweet flower.

response.speaker: Jack
response.text: Put the sweet flower in the bottom of a glass, then pour the beer over it. Shake it up a bit to work up a head.

response.speaker: Jack
response.text: Then comes the good part — glugging away to your heart's content! Easy enough eh?

response.speaker: Jack
response.text: Go on, get your drinking cap on!

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: The idea of my signature drink being served at the Angel's Share... Hard to explain how it feels...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: If I was to choose a drink to mix, I'd need to think about it. What was my favorite tipple again...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: What to mix with beer, hmm... Trial and error, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: How is it going? Ready to mix it up?

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Choose your base.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Wow... I've never seen a drink quite like this before. I bet it tastes great...

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Mmm, very good! I will remember this recipe... I hope my customers will like it. Thanks, traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Maybe some of the customers will like it. Thanks, traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: I... I appreciate all your efforts, but I just can't see most people enjoying a drink like this. I'll have another think. Thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Traveler... Please learn to rein in your creative excesses in future.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Though you're a beginner, you should have no problem with one of the Drunkards guiding you every step of the way.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Ooh... The sweetness of the freshly squeezed fruit really takes the edge off of the fiery liquor. It goes down smooth, but still has a kick to it.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: This is some masterful mixology right here! I could serve this Mondstadt Sunset as-is! But where does it get its name?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: If you look carefully, you can see the fruit juices settling in the liquor. Don't you think it looks like the view from Starsnatch Cliff at sundown as the sunlight pours out over Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Whew, this drink doesn't pull any punches... If anything, the cool of the dandelion seeds seems to add to the fieriness of the liquor! My tongue is numb, but I can't tell whether it's the burn or the chill...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Hey! This is just straight liquor — you call this mixing a drink!?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: What a novel sensation. Thick foam, refreshing beer and some crushed sweet flower too... A session beer through and through!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: The taste is passable at best, but just look how beautiful it is... The key to making a good Mondstadt Sunset, apart from making sure it's well shaken and stirred, is to let it sit long enough for the juices to settle...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: This is... just straight liquor, no? I can't see anything special about it.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Which is why I ask, how can you call this a mixed drink?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Ooh... The texture is like that of regular beer, but where is that residue coming from? Did you put something in it?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Haha... Whatever this is, it sure isn't a Mondstadt Sunrise! You used the wrong ingredients, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: ...This is just straight liquor!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Oi! At least put something else in the mix. All this is is straight liquor!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Haha, gotta love a good old beer— Hang on, what's this sediment doing in here...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: What in Teyvat have you put in this!? My tongue is all numb!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: My oh my... That was simply— Oh no! It's all gone...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Make me another, won't you? Just one more, just like the last one... Please!

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Hmm... Nothing to write home about. But surprisingly good for a beginner!

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: A very pleasant taste, but you've put too much mixer in and I can barely taste the alcohol. It's more of a fruit juice than an alcoholic beverage. I bet Diona would like it...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: It's looking good. Why no other ingredients? That's because it's my house special, the Margaret.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Jagerschnapps infused with freshly picked dandelion seeds... Savor that cold rush as it hits your tongue...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: A glass of this down the tavern late at night perks you up instantly, giving you the presence of mind to deal judiciously with any smooth-talking new acquaintances...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Berries to balance the flavor... A novel approach. But if my customers drank this they'd either collapse in a drunken stupor or walk straight back out of the tavern...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Flavored beer — definitely a thing... But with a head like this you need to drink it up pronto, because if you let the foam disappear then the taste and texture will suffer.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: I can taste that it's a fruity cocktail. But I can't tell anything else about it from looking at it.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: You can tell it's more than just straight liquor, but the Dandelion Seed flavor isn't coming through at all, probably because of an incorrect mixing technique. My tavern wouldn't stay in business much longer if this was what the Margaret tasted like.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Why are there so many air bubbles in a glass of straight liquor? It creates a fairly disgusting sensation...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: The head doesn't feel right somehow, and a bad head kind of ruins a good beer...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Is this supposed to be a fruity cocktail? I am a little underwhelmed.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: You forgot what goes in a Margaret, didn't you? Whatever you've made here is completely different...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Yeugh... This is actually disgusting...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: It's beer, plain and simple. And boring.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Get that thing away from me! It's destroying my sense of smell...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: #Wow, this... Hey {NICKNAME}, how would you like to work at the Cat's Tail?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: In addition to a generous salary package, you'd have the pleasure of working alongside Diona every day... Give it some thought!

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: This is the same as what I drink every day. Nothing exceptional, nothing wrong with it either. Alcoholic and drinkable.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: There's not a whiff of alcohol in this! I'll tell you who this drink's for — big sissy girls, that's who! You certainly won't catch me drinking this in front of the other hunters...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Booyah! That'll perk you up alright. One of these before the hunt... Mm-hmm!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Now we're talking! A short, sharp shock that leaves you feeling warm and fuzzy all over.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Gets you ready to make a charged attack on any prey that comes your way. Here's to hunting, and here's to drinking! Hunters, look alive!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Beer...? Hmm, it's alright once in a while I s'pose...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Fruit-based beverages taste grim... and this one looks grim, too. Get rid of it.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: There's definitely liquor in there, but what's all that other stuff... Why'd you need to complicate it so much when you can just drink it as-is?

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Oi, you didn't overdo it on the shaking and stirring, did you? No wonder the texture's all wrong... The body of even straight liquor suffers when you move it about too much. ...But it's still drinkable, I guess.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Beer? Can't go too wrong with the odd beer.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: There is no point in drinking this whatsoever.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: It'd be alright without all that other gunk in there, but... As it stands, it's a bit of a chore to drink!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Don't put such random stuff in there, it ruins the flavor of the alcohol!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Phew... I can't taste what makes this different from regular beer... Get me another! I'll give it another try...

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: It's nearly hunting time, I shouldn't have any more.

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: One more please... In fact, get me a few of these to go! I want all the hunters in Springvale to try it!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: This is nothing special. I could have made this myself!

dialogues.speaker: Draff
dialogues.text: Phwoar, that tastes great! ...But you can barely feel it on the way down. It doesn't have that buzz to it.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: What did you... I... I can't feel my tongue...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Sorry, but I've had a sip and... And one sip is quite enough for me!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: The best part of a beer is that first sip, right after cheersing with a mate! After that first sip of foam with bits of sweet flower in, the stress of the day just melts away.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Look at the bits of overflowing foam — don't they look like pearls? Cheers...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: I forgot — you're not old enough. Get yourself an apple vinegar then. This one's on me!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Here's a tip. If you want people to actually drink what you put in front of them, it has to look and feel like a genuine drink...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Is this... straight liquor? And if so, what's that floating around in it?

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Straight up liquor...? I think I'll pass, thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: I can't fault the flavor — but the foam, and as a result the texture... It doesn't exactly scream of friends drinking together and having a good time; more like something you'd drown your sorrows with. What went wrong? ...Then again, since you took the trouble to make it...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: This is basically the same as every other fruit-juice-centric cocktail I've ever had.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Yeugh... This is actually disgusting. Whatever you added just made it worse

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Yeugh... This is actually disgusting. Whatever you added just made it worse

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: This thick head of foam all but masks a unique and subtle flavor... I can't tell what it is, but it certainly isn't sweet flower.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Even the bravest of adventurers wouldn't dare touch this stuff!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Wow... this is really something. Shame you're not allowed to drink yet!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: It's a travesty not to be able to share this fine drink with someone else...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: This tastes decidedly... average. But there's certainly nothing wrong with it.
